author: odiseolook19
quote: Visually, it’s insane, and Leonida is easily the most alive and detailed map I have ever stepped foot in. However, after more than 40 hours, it’s painfully clear that this is no longer the irreverent Grand Theft Auto that made us fall in love with the series. Rockstar has traded its razor-sharp satire and unfiltered dark humor for a watered-down, shallow brand of comedy designed purely to generate quick TikTok **** previous entries, the game took shots at everyone without ever worrying about making people uncomfortable; here, you can feel the handbrake pulled from the very first minute. The writing would rather poke fun at easy, safe targets—generic influencers, crypto scammers, or internet weirdos—than deliver any genuinely biting social commentary. Everything feels overly sanitized, as if the dialogue had been run through a thousand corporate filters just to make sure nobody gets offended. Dan Houser's absence in the writing room is glaringly obvious: the relationship between Jason and Lucia works well on a dramatic level, but the world completely lacks that cynical edge and adult grit that made the radio stations and side missions so **** to that the fact that the game is locked at 30 fps with no performance mode, and that the obsession with realism slows down basic fun like starting a shootout or losing the cops, and the whole experience ends up feeling more like a chore than a blast. It is an undeniable technological marvel, sure, but as a GTA game, it feels tamed and stripped of its personality.
